title: preview
rule: Show a preview or summary of what will happen when the user performs the action.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Preview (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: A preview or summary of the result is available before the person commits.
fail_when: The action commits with no preview or summary of what will happen.
overview: A preview or summary shows what will happen before the person commits.
apply_when: Committing an action whose result is hard to imagine without a sample.
not_when: Trivial commits whose outcome is already obvious from the label alone.
agent_hint: Offer a preview or summary of the result before commit when outcomes are opaque.
description: Show a preview or summary of what will happen before commit when the result is hard to picture from the label alone. Committing blind forces undo, redo, or regret after the fact. Use preview for consequential or visually opaque changes so people can judge the outcome first. Skip it when the outcome is already crystal clear from the control wording and context.
